clue.text: Play jealous husband to return greeting

indicators.note: to return means the little word to is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned round
hello is an everyday greeting

explanation.surface: An actor is told to come back on stage and say hello in the role of a jealous husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns TO into OT; then add HELLO. The definition names both Shakespeare's play and its title character, the husband driven to murder by jealousy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy is named after its Moorish general, whose jealousy leads him to kill his wife Desdemona.

clue.text: Seat of an empire

explanation.surface: A throne at the centre of an imperial power.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded footstool or couch is so called, and the Turkish empire of the sultans bore the same dynastic name.

clue.text: Cite her conversion as a dissenter

indicators.note: a conversion changes something into another form, so these letters are remade

explanation.surface: A churchman quotes a woman's religious conversion as proof that she rejects doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds beliefs contrary to accepted church doctrine is a dissenter from orthodoxy.

clue.text: As a passenger carrier I get involved with former railway

indicators.note: getting involved with something puts one inside it, so the I goes within the railway's letters

parts.note: LNER was the London and North Eastern Railway, a British company before nationalisation

explanation.surface: Someone talks about joining an old railway company as a carrier of passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: LNER was one of Britain's big four railway companies before 1948; I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean-going ship that carries travellers on a regular route is a large passenger vessel.

clue.text: Unreasonably persistent idea for an old boys' gathering

parts.note: OB is the usual abbreviation for an old boy, a former pupil of a school
a session is a meeting or gathering of people

explanation.surface: A school reunion becomes a fixation for those who cannot let go.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one OB is needed: the possessive 'old boys'' just says the gathering belongs to former pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixation that occupies the mind beyond reason is what a psychologist would call a compulsive preoccupation.

clue.text: The old ensign is really old

explanation.surface: A veteran standard-bearer is genuinely aged.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's day an ancient was an ensign or standard-bearer: Iago in Othello is 'Othello's ancient'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a flag-bearer, and also an adjective for something of great age.

clue.text: Superficial extents are as written here

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note explains how surface measurements are recorded in this document.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's own words 'are as', written here run together, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Extents of a surface, measured in square units, are its regions or expanses.

clue.text: The Royal yacht, for instance, could lead to an engagement

explanation.surface: Sailing on the monarch's yacht might end in a proposal of marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as COURT SHIP, the royal yacht is a ship of the court; as one word it is wooing.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel belonging to the royal household, and also the period of wooing that precedes a betrothal.

clue.text: Oriental movement concerned with disturbance of mind

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient
motion is movement

explanation.surface: An eastern political movement is concerned with mental unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong feeling such as anger or grief is an agitation of the mind.

clue.text: Do they try out bed canopies for old money?

explanation.surface: A question about whether people trial four-poster canopies in exchange for old coins.
explanation.walkthrough: A tester is a canopy over a four-poster bed, and also an old English sixpence or shilling.
explanation.definitionFit: People who trial things, overhead canopies on old beds, and Tudor silver coins all share the name.

clue.text: Seats of the mighty holding one

definitions.text: Seats of the mighty holding one

parts.words: Seats of the mighty holding one
parts.note: the grand chairs of kings and queens, each made to hold a single ruler

explanation.surface: Grand chairs of powerful rulers, each with room for one person.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremonial chairs of state occupied by monarchs, each seating a lone sovereign.

clue.text: With Australia's big bird in front, behold us, eager to copy!

indicators.note: in front tells us the bird's letters lead the rest

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
lo is an old word meaning behold
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation inviting us to look at Australia's big bird and imitate it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone keen to rival or imitate another is filled with emulation.

clue.text: Most riots are dispersed by such road users

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Drivers break up most riots by driving through.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers of cars are users of the highway.

clue.text: Edible nonsense!

explanation.surface: An exclamation that something eatable is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The stomach lining of cattle is eaten as offal, and the word is also slang for rubbishy talk.

clue.text: Audible blows are at least top notch for toxophilites

indicators.note: audible means heard, so the word for blows is said out loud

parts.note: knocks are blows

explanation.surface: Archers hear resounding blows and rate them excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: Toxophilites are archers; a nock is the notch at the end of an arrow or bow for the string. 'Top notch' looks like 'excellent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Archers call the small groove cut in the arrow's tail, which sits on the bowstring, by this name.

clue.text: Petticoat for a cricketer

explanation.surface: An undergarment for a cricket player.
explanation.walkthrough: Short slip is a cricket fielding position close to the batsman, beside the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief underskirt, and a fielder placed in the slips close behind the bat in cricket.

clue.text: There's proverbial diabolical mischief to be wrought by lazy workers

definitions.text: There's proverbial diabolical mischief to be wrought by lazy workers

parts.words: There's proverbial diabolical mischief to be wrought by lazy workers
parts.note: points to the saying that the devil finds work for people with nothing to do

explanation.surface: A proverb warns that idle labourers get up to devilish mischief.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'the devil makes work for unoccupied fingers' names the hands of the lazy.

clue.text: Most modern paintings made by a tardy traveller

parts.note: latest means most recent or most modern
art covers paintings

explanation.surface: A traveller running late produces the newest paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as LATEST ART it is the newest painting; as LATE START it is what a tardy traveller makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sets off behind schedule begins a journey belatedly.

clue.text: Poem about sliced bun helps to keep a cool head

definitions.text: helps to keep a cool head

indicators.note: about means around, so the poem's letters go round the others

parts.note: a sonnet is a fourteen-line poem

indicators.note: sliced means cut up, so the letters of bun are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poem about a sliced bun helps someone stay calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sliced' rearranges the bun's letters and 'about' wraps the poem round them, just after its first letter. 'cool head' suggests calm; it is literal shade from the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed cotton hat shades the wearer from the heat of the sun.

clue.text: Herbal remedies could be the easy ones

explanation.surface: Plant-based cures might be the simple ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicinal herbs were called this in old herbalism, and the word also means uncomplicated things.

clue.text: Famous but unskilled

explanation.surface: Someone renowned yet incompetent.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NOT ABLE it means lacking skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinguished and well known, and also, split in two, incapable.

clue.text: Cuts down braces, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a brace is a pair, so braces are pairs

explanation.surface: Someone trims their trouser braces, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim or reduce, as with a knife on fruit skin.

clue.text: Three thirds of old Yorkshire

parts.note: the historic English county was split into North, East and West divisions, each named from an Old Norse word for a third

explanation.surface: The three parts that made up the old county of Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire, a large county in northern England, was divided until 1974 into three administrative parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The three historic divisions of the county take their name from Old Norse thrithjungr, a third part.

clue.text: Masters disturbed by little flowers

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Schoolmasters are upset by small blossoms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' wants to be blooms; here it means things that flow.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooks and rivulets are small things that flow, with flower read as one that flows.

clue.text: Church anthem taken from remote text

indicators.note: taken from means the letters are lifted out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A hymn sung in church comes from an obscure document.
explanation.definitionFit: A short polyphonic choral setting of sacred words is sung in church services.

clue.text: Equipment for a hold up at the hosier's

definitions.text: Equipment for a hold up at the hosier's

parts.words: Equipment for a hold up at the hosier's
parts.note: a stocking shop sells gear that keeps stockings up, read as if a robbery were planned

explanation.surface: Gear for a robbery at a shop that sells stockings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold up' suggests a robbery; it is the strap that holds stockings or socks up.
explanation.definitionFit: An elastic strap attached to a belt keeps stockings in place.

clue.text: Singular step made plurally in case

definitions.text: Singular step made plurally in case

parts.words: Singular step made plurally in case
parts.note: one step of a flight; many of them, set inside a casing, make the whole flight between floors

explanation.surface: A single step that, multiplied, forms a flight inside a casing.
explanation.walkthrough: One step is the singular; the plural, with CASE added, names the whole flight with its enclosing structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step in a flight leading from floor to floor.

clue.text: Little whirlpool heard by Ted perhaps

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken aloud, not spelt

parts.note: an eddy is a small whirlpool

explanation.surface: A small whirlpool is listened to by a man called Ted.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted and the answer are both pet forms of the name Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are familiar short forms of Edward, so a Ted could also be known by this name.

clue.text: Lamb is after a high ball in the garden

indicators.note: is after puts the second piece behind the first

parts.note: a lob is a ball hit high
Elia was the pen name of essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A lamb chases a ball tossed high in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb wrote his Essays of Elia under that name; 'Lamb' looks like the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailing blue-flowered plant grown in garden beds and hanging baskets.

clue.text: Roughly added an appendix or two

definitions.note: plural sense: more than one supplement

indicators.note: roughly means imprecisely, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hastily tacked on an appendix or two.
explanation.definitionFit: Items added at the end of a book are supplements, here in the Latin plural.

clue.text: Somnolent one holds up the line for British Rail

definitions.text: holds up the line for British Rail

explanation.surface: A drowsy person delays a train on the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: On British railways the beams under the rails are called sleepers (US: ties).
explanation.definitionFit: A dozing person, and the wooden or concrete beam that supports railway track.

clue.text: Locksfornazisecretpolice in the woodland

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: woodland is made of trees
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary force; the words are printed run together

explanation.surface: Hair grows wild where Nazi police hide in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Locks for nazi secret police' run together as one word; 'in' signals the container, and the definition is 'Locks', meaning hair rather than fastenings.
explanation.definitionFit: Long locks of hair are flowing tresses.
